subject: Post-demo: deployment mode & isolation follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sofie Nørgaard <sofie@finpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: deployment mode & isolation follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Sofie — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Your primary constraints: 99.9% uptime target for peak hours, strict data residency in the Netherlands, and procurement preference for a single vendor for both API and infra.
- We showed Hosted API for fastest ramp, Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation, Private (VPC/on-prem) for stricter control and auditability.

Key open questions you raised (I wanted to put these in writing so we can address them concretely):
1) Isolation/Noisy neighbor: you asked whether customers on Hosted API share GPU pools and what mitigations exist for noisy-neighbor impact on latency during peak bursts.
2) SLO guarantees: whether the SLOs differ materially between Hosted and Dedicated offerings and what remedies/redress look like.
3) Data boundary assurances for the Private option: KMS/HSM integration and audit logs availability.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- I will attach a short note comparing isolation behaviors between Hosted & Dedicated, and include a snapshot of our SOC2 summary. (attached)
- Karthik (cc) can lead a quick technical deep-dive if you want to validate tail-latency and isolation details with your infra team.
- Monica (cc) will follow up with an updated Dedicated pricing PDF that includes reserve/burst options and an outline of SLA targets.

Are you available for a 30-min technical deep-dive on Thu or Fri this week? If you prefer, we can start with a 15-min sync just on isolation SLOs and then expand.

Thanks — Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf (summary pricing), redwood-soc2-summary-2025.txt (one-page SOC2 snapshot)

From: Sofie Nørgaard <sofie@finpay.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@finpay.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment mode & isolation follow-up (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Dylan — thanks for the recap and attachments. A few clarifications from our side: 

On noisy neighbor and Hosted API:
- We are worried about tail-latency spikes during end-of-month settlement windows. If other tenants suddenly surge, will our 95th/99th pct latency spike? How do you protect latency-sensitive endpoints on Hosted?

On Dedicated vs Private:
- Dedicated sounds appealing if it gives hardware-level isolation (i.e., reserved GPU pools) and predictable throughput. But procurement will push back on the cost unless we can quantify expected tail-latency and percent of requests that will be on-prem-like latencies.

On SLOs and remedies:
- We need to understand typical SLO targets (p95/p99 token latency) per deployment mode and what financial or operational remedies are offered for breaches.

Finally, our security team would like to see specifics about KMS and audit log retention for the Private option — retention windows and export controls.

If Thu/ Fri works, I prefer Fri morning CET. I’ll loop in our infra lead if we do a technical deep-dive.

— Sofie
Head of Platform Engineering, FinPay

Hi Sofie — thanks for the detailed notes. Short answers now, we can expand on the call Friday CET: 

1) Hosted noisy-neighbor protections (summary):
- Multi-tenant pool but with workload-aware routing: latency-sensitive endpoints can be routed to lower-utilization pools.
- Prefix/KV cache and adaptive batching reduce per-token load for repeatable requests.
- Continuous tail-latency monitoring + automated short-term routing to spare capacity; this mitigates most p95 spikes during short bursts. For very long, sustained surges we fallback to compatible model variants or Dedicated where needed.

2) Dedicated guarantees:
- Hardware isolation via reserved GPU pools (no co-tenancy at the GPU card level for reserved seats).
- Predictable throughput and a documented latency profile (we’ll share real-world p95/p99 numbers from comparable customers).
- SLA options: standard (99.9% uptime) and premium (99.95% with credits). Remedies include service credits and escalation playbooks — details in the Dedicated pricing PDF.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem) & security controls:
- Full control plane in your VPC, KMS integration for key custody, and configurable audit log retention.
- On-prem option supports HSM via our agent; logs can be exported to your SIEM.

Action items: 
- Karthik: can you prepare a 1-pager with example p95/p99 latency numbers from two customers with similar batch patterns? (we need anonymized figures).
- Monica: can you add a short SLA summary to the pricing PDF and call out reserved GPU seat sizing guidance?
- Dylan: I’ll book Fri 09:30 CET / 08:30 UK as a tentative slot for the tech deep-dive — Sofie, please confirm if that works.

Thanks — Dylan
